# neo-pi - bare metal Neo Geo emulator (Raspberry Pi 4 / 400 and Raspberry Pi 3)
arm_64bit=1
kernel_address=0x80000
initial_turbo=0

# Picture even if the TV is switched on after the Pi; no extra black border
hdmi_force_hotplug=1
disable_overscan=1
# HDMI with audio; pixels always opaque
hdmi_drive=2
framebuffer_ignore_alpha=1

# Fixed output, 1920x1080 at 60 Hz (also on 4K TVs: the TV scales it up).
# If your screen does not accept it, put a # in front of the next two lines:
# the screen's preferred mode will be used.
hdmi_group=1
hdmi_mode=16
# 1280x720 at 60 Hz instead: put a # in front of hdmi_mode=16 and remove it here.
# At 720p the 3x enlargement is done by the CPU alone.
#hdmi_mode=4

# Hardware scaler (HVS): sharp pixels, no smoothing
scaling_kernel=8

# HDMI CEC: name shown in the TV's source list. At start-up the firmware also
# asks the TV to switch to this input (if CEC is enabled on the TV).
cec_osd_name=NEO-PI

# Faster, cleaner start-up: no rainbow screen, no 1 second wait before the
# kernel, no HAT EEPROM probing
disable_splash=1
boot_delay=0
force_eeprom_read=0
# Fixed GPU core clock: no clock changes while playing
core_freq_fixed=1

[pi3]
kernel=kernel8.img
# Mild overclock: remove the # to try it
#arm_freq=1300

[pi3+]
kernel=kernel8.img
#arm_freq=1500

[pi4]
armstub=armstub8-rpi4.bin
kernel=kernel8-rpi4.img
max_framebuffers=2
# Overclock (needs a good heatsink and the official power supply):
# remove the # to try it. A Pi 400 can take arm_freq=2100.
#arm_freq=1900

[all]
